official_sources.title: NumPy peak-to-peak signed-integer overflow warning
official_sources.finding: NumPy defines peak-to-peak as maximum minus minimum but preserves the input dtype; signed integer ranges exceeding the dtype can therefore wrap and appear negative.
official_sources.limitation: Casting the final wrapped result is too late; extrema operands must be promoted before subtraction.

official_sources.title: NumPy discrete-difference unsigned wrap behavior
official_sources.finding: NumPy documents that unsigned differences remain unsigned and may wrap, and recommends casting to a larger signed type before differencing when wrap is not desired.
official_sources.limitation: A generic larger integer is not always sufficient when scale, offset or floating decoding is involved.

official_sources.title: NumPy subtract dtype, broadcasting and where semantics
official_sources.finding: NumPy subtract supports an explicit output dtype and broadcasting; with a newly allocated output, locations excluded by where remain uninitialized.
official_sources.limitation: Broadcast-compatible shapes can still represent the wrong extrema pairing, so scalar and pair identifiers must be pinned.

official_sources.title: NumPy result-type promotion rules
official_sources.finding: NumPy result_type reports the dtype obtained from its promotion rules for the supplied operands and dtypes.
official_sources.limitation: The inferred result type is a diagnostic, not an acceptance policy; the workflow must require a reviewed minimum safe dtype.

official_sources.title: NumPy spacing adjacent representable-value distance
official_sources.finding: NumPy spacing returns the distance from a finite value to its nearest adjacent representable floating-point number.
official_sources.limitation: ULP distance characterizes representation granularity, not source measurement accuracy or vertical-datum uncertainty.

official_sources.title: NumPy nextafter adjacent-value direction
official_sources.finding: NumPy nextafter returns the next representable floating-point value after one value in the direction of another.
official_sources.limitation: A one-ULP probe detects representational boundaries but cannot justify tolerance-based merging of distinct elevations.

official_sources.title: NumPy sign-bit inspection
official_sources.finding: NumPy signbit reports whether the sign bit is set, allowing positive and negative zero representations to be distinguished.
official_sources.limitation: Normalizing negative zero is a serialization rule and must not alter any nonzero signed result.

official_sources.title: Python itertools Cartesian-product ordering
official_sources.finding: itertools.product forms the Cartesian product as nested loops and emits lexicographically when the input iterables are sorted.
official_sources.limitation: Materializing every pair can be expensive; streaming, pair-count reconciliation and deterministic digests remain required.
